name: com.amaltash/calculators
title: Amaltash Investment & Retirement Calculators
description: Compound interest, CD, 401(k), Roth IRA, RMD, amortization and mortgage payoff calculators.

tools.name: plan_recurring_investment
tools.description: Investment calculator with an interactive chart. Works out what regular deposits could grow to at a long-run market average or a yearly rate you choose. Use it for monthly investment plans and questions like what $10 a day or $500 a month could become in 20 or 30 years. Single stocks cannot be run forward. People ask for it as "investment calculator", "investment growth calculator" or "how much should i invest each month".

amount.description: Dollars put in each time, above 0.

cadence.description: How often the amount goes in.

asset.description: A long-run rate to use. Give this or custom_annual_percent, not both.

custom_annual_percent.description: Your own yearly return in percent, so 7 means 7%. Give this or asset, not both.

tools.name: list_assets
tools.description: Lists the long-run market rates, which can be used for future plans, and common stocks and funds, which can only be used to look at the past. Stock questions work for any US stock or fund we hold history for, past only. Use it to find a valid long-run rate id.

tools.name: replay_past_investing
tools.description: Stock return and dollar-cost averaging (DCA) calculator with an interactive chart. Shows what investing in a US stock or fund would have become, using real past prices, as regular deposits, a lump sum, or both. Use it for what-if-I-had-invested and DCA questions about a ticker such as AAPL or VOO, over the last 120 months or fewer. It covers the past only and gives no estimate of the future. People ask for it as "stock profit calculator", "dollar cost averaging calculator" or "what if i invested".

ticker.description: A US stock or fund ticker, such as AAPL or SPY.

amount.description: Dollars invested each time. Can be 0 if there is a starting amount.

cadence.description: How often the amount goes in: day, week or month. Defaults to month.

starting_amount.description: Dollars invested once at the start. Defaults to 0.

months_back.description: How many months before the latest data to begin, from 1 to 120.

tools.name: sp500_since_date
tools.description: S&P 500 return calculator with an interactive chart. Shows what a set amount in the S&P 500 would have become between two years from 1928 to 2025, using real yearly returns. It also gives the amount put in after inflation and the worst year in the span. People ask for it as "s&p 500 calculator", "s&p 500 investment calculator" or "s&p 500 return calculator".

cadence.description: How often the money goes in: day, week, month, year, or once.

to_year.description: Last year, included, from 1928 to 2025. Cannot be before from_year.

tools.name: retirement_plan
tools.description: Retirement calculator with an interactive chart of the balance by age. Replays a plan through every complete stretch of real US market history since 1928 and reports how often the money lasted. Use it when the monthly spending is known, for questions like can I retire at 60, or how long will my savings last. People ask for it as "retirement calculator", "how much money do i need to retire" or "can i retire at 62".

age.description: Age today, in whole years, from 18 to 100.

retire_age.description: Age when saving stops and spending starts. It cannot be below age.

end_age.description: Age the money must last to. It must be above retire_age, and the span from age must fit in the data since 1928.

savings.description: Money saved so far, in US dollars.

save_monthly.description: Dollars added each month until retirement.

other_income.description: Monthly income in retirement from other sources, such as Social Security, in today's dollars.

stock.description: Share held in stocks, from 0 to 1. The rest is in 10-year US Treasuries.

spend_monthly.description: Monthly spending in retirement, in today's dollars.

tools.name: safe_spending
tools.description: Retirement withdrawal calculator with an interactive chart. Finds the highest monthly spending that lasted in at least a chosen share of real US market history since 1928. Use it when the spending amount is the unknown, for retirement income questions, and to check the 4% rule.

age.description: Age today, in whole years, from 18 to 100.

retire_age.description: Age when saving stops and spending starts. It cannot be below age.

end_age.description: Age the money must last to. It must be above retire_age, and the span from age must fit in the data since 1928.

savings.description: Money saved so far, in US dollars.

save_monthly.description: Dollars added each month until retirement.

other_income.description: Monthly income in retirement from other sources, such as Social Security, in today's dollars.

stock.description: Share held in stocks, from 0 to 1. The rest is in 10-year US Treasuries.

share.description: Share of past periods the money must last in, from 0.5 to 1.

tools.name: compound_interest
tools.description: Compound interest calculator with an interactive chart. Works out what a starting amount and monthly deposits grow to at a fixed rate, compounded daily, monthly or yearly, and gives the APY. Use it for savings growth, CD and high-yield savings balances, future value at a fixed rate, and questions like what $10,000 becomes in 10 years at 5%. People ask for it as "compound interest calculator", "daily compound interest calculator" or "how to calculate compound interest".

per_month.description: Dollars added at the end of each month.

annual_rate_percent.description: Yearly interest rate as a percent, so 5 means 5%.

compounding.description: How often interest is added to the balance.

tools.name: net_worth_check
tools.description: Net worth calculator with an interactive chart. Subtracts debts from assets and, when an age is given, shows the median net worth for that age group from a US government survey. Use it for a net worth total or a net worth by age comparison. People ask for it as "net worth calculator", "net worth by age calculator" or "what is my net worth".

assets.description: Total value of everything owned, in US dollars.

debts.description: Total of everything owed, as a positive number of US dollars.

age.description: Age in whole years, from 18 to 110, to compare with others that age.

tools.name: crash_impact
tools.description: Portfolio stress test with an interactive chart. Works out how much a portfolio would lose if stocks fell by a chosen percent, given its mix of stocks, bonds and cash, with an optional loss limit.

portfolio_value.description: Total portfolio value in US dollars.

stocks_pct.description: Share of the portfolio in stocks, in percent. Stocks, bonds and cash must add up to 100.

bonds_pct.description: Share of the portfolio in bonds, in percent.

cash_pct.description: Share of the portfolio in cash, in percent.

stock_crash_pct.description: How far stocks fall, in percent, from 0 to 100.

drawdown_limit_pct.description: Optional limit on the portfolio loss, in percent of the portfolio. Leave null for no limit.

tools.name: drawdown_recovery
tools.description: Drawdown and loss recovery calculator with an interactive chart. Works out the percentage gain needed to get back to even after a loss, and how many years that takes at a yearly return the person enters.

loss_pct.description: The loss, in percent, from 0 up to but not including 100.

annual_return_pct.description: Optional yearly return, in percent, used to estimate years to recover. Leave null to skip the estimate.

tools.name: sequence_risk
tools.description: Sequence of returns calculator with an interactive chart. Runs a list of yearly returns with a fixed yearly withdrawal in the order given and in reverse, and compares where the balance ends.

annual_withdrawal.description: Amount withdrawn at the start of each year, in US dollars.

items.description: One yearly return in percent, above -100.

returns_pct.description: Yearly returns in percent, in order, from 1 to 60 years.

tools.name: position_size
tools.description: Position size calculator with an interactive chart. Works out the dollar size of one position at a percent cap the person chooses, how many positions of that size fit, and the amount at risk. It does not pick investments or judge whether a size is suitable.

portfolio_value.description: Total portfolio value in US dollars.

max_position_pct.description: The cap per position or theme, in percent of the portfolio, the person chose.

stop_distance_pct.description: Optional stop distance below entry, in percent. Leave null if there is none.

tools.name: dca_vs_lump_sum
tools.description: Dollar-cost averaging vs lump sum calculator with an interactive chart. Compares investing a fixed amount at each price in a list with investing the same total at the first price, both valued at the last price. Use it when the person provides the price series.

amount_per_period.description: Dollars invested at each price, from 0 to 1,000,000,000.

items.description: The price for one period, above 0.

prices.description: One price per period, oldest first, from 1 to 120 prices.

tools.name: tbill_ladder
tools.description: Treasury bill ladder calculator with an interactive timeline chart. Lays out how much goes in each same-term bill, how far apart to buy them, and the first and last dates. Shows simple interest only if a rate is given.

amount.description: Total dollars to split across the bills, from 0 to 1,000,000,000.

rungs.description: How many bills to stagger, a whole number no larger than the term in weeks (13 at most for 52-week bills).

term_weeks.description: Length of each bill in weeks: 4, 8, 13, 17, 26 or 52.

start_date.description: The first purchase date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

rate_pct.description: An annual interest rate the person chooses, in percent, from 0 to 25. Leave out to skip interest.

tools.name: calculate_cd_interest
tools.description: CD Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How much will your CD earn? A CD, or certificate of deposit, is a bank account that pays a set rate for a set time. It adds interest at the CD rate you type, for the whole term, as often as you pick. It does not look up the rates banks pay today. People ask for it as "cd calculator", "cd rate calculator" or "how much interest does a cd earn".

start.description: Money you put in. US dollars. Default: 10000.

rate.description: CD rate each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Your bank’s rate. Treasury bills averaged 3.4%, 1928–2025. Default: 3.4.

years.description: Years until the CD ends. In years. Whole years only. Default: 5.

n.description: How often interest is added. Your bank’s terms say which. Default: 365.

tools.name: price_treasury_bill
tools.description: T-Bill Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What does a Treasury bill cost and pay? A Treasury bill, or T-bill, is a short loan to the US government. You pay a little less now and get the full amount back later. It prices a bill from the rate you type, using the Treasury’s discount math. It can also lay out a ladder of bills with dates. It does not buy bills or show live auction results. People ask for it as "t bill calculator", "treasury bill calculator" or "how do treasury bills work".

amount.description: Money you get back. US dollars. You pay a little less now. Default: 40000.

bills.description: Number of bills. 2 or more pay you back in turns. Default: 4.

rate.description: Interest rate each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Use today’s rate. 3-month bills averaged 3.4%, 1928–2025. Default: 3.4.

kind.description: Kind of rate. Treasury results list both. Default: investment.

tools.name: project_savings_growth
tools.description: High-Yield Savings Account Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How much will your savings earn? A high-yield savings account pays more interest than most. You can add or take out money any time, but the rate can change. It adds interest at the rate you type, with the money you add each month. It does not know what rate a bank will pay. Real savings rates can change at any time. People ask for it as "high yield savings account calculator", "hysa calculator" or "savings interest calculator".

start.description: Money in savings now. US dollars. Default: 10000.

add.description: Money you add each month. US dollars. Default: 200.

rate.description: Interest rate each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Your bank’s rate. Treasury bills averaged 3.4%, 1928–2025. Default: 3.4.

years.description: How many years. In years. Default: 5.

n.description: How often interest is added. Your bank’s terms say which. Default: 365.

tools.name: plan_emergency_fund
tools.description: Emergency Fund Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How much should you keep for emergencies? An emergency fund is cash for surprise bills or a loss of pay. See your goal and how long it takes. It multiplies your monthly costs by the months you pick. Then it counts the months to save that much at your pace. It does not pick the right size for you. There is no one right number. People ask for it as "emergency fund calculator", "how much emergency fund should i have" or "how much should i have in an emergency fund".

costs.description: Must-pay costs each month. US dollars. Rent, food, power, insurance, debt payments Default: 3200.

months.description: Months to cover. In months. Default: 3.

saved.description: Saved so far. US dollars. Default: 1500.

perMonth.description: You save each month. US dollars. Default: 400.

apy.description: Savings rate (APY). A percent: 5 means 5%. Your account’s rate. 0 leaves interest out. Default: 0.

income.description: Money still coming in each month. US dollars. A partner’s pay or jobless benefits Default: 0.

tools.name: convert_apr_to_apy
tools.description: APR to APY Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What is my APR as an APY? APR is a yearly rate that leaves out interest on interest. APY counts it, so it shows what the rate adds up to in a year. It turns an APR into an APY by adding interest on interest as often as you pick. It can also go the other way. It does not count fees, which can change what a loan really costs. People ask for it as "apr vs apy", "how is apy calculated" or "apr to apy calculator".

from.description: The rate you have. Default: apr.

rate.description: Your rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. From your statement, loan papers or bank. Default: 20.

n.description: How often interest is added. Default: 365.

balance.description: Balance, owed or saved. US dollars. Optional. Shows one year of interest. Default: 1000.

tools.name: calculate_simple_interest
tools.description: Simple Interest Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How much interest on a loan or deposit? Simple interest is worked out only on the amount you start with. The interest never earns interest of its own. It works out interest on the starting amount only: amount times rate times time. It does not add interest on interest. People ask for it as "simple interest calculator", "how to calculate interest on a loan per day" or "how to calculate simple interest on a loan".

p.description: Amount. US dollars. The amount lent, borrowed or saved. Default: 6000.

r.description: Interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Use the rate on your loan or account. Default: 3.4.

unit.description: Count the time in. Default: years.

per.description: The rate is for. Default: year.

basis.description: Days in a year. Only for days. Some banks use 360. Default: 365.

tools.name: estimate_doubling_time
tools.description: Rule of 72 Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How long until my money doubles? The rule of 72 is a quick guess: 72 ÷ the yearly rate is about how many years it takes to double. It divides 72 by the yearly rate for a quick guess. Then it shows the exact time to double at that rate. It does not say what rate your money will earn. People ask for it as "rule of 72", "rule of 72 calculator" or "how long to double money".

rate.description: Yearly rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Like the rate on savings or a loan. Default: 4.

amount.description: Money you start with. US dollars. This only changes the chart. Default: 1000.

tools.name: calculate_apy
tools.description: APY Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What is my APY? APY is what a rate really pays in a year. It counts interest earned on interest. It turns a rate into its APY by counting interest on interest as often as you pick. It also shows a year of interest. It does not look up the rates banks pay today. People ask for it as "apy calculator", "how is apy calculated" or "how do i calculate apy".

rate.description: Interest rate each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. The rate before interest on interest. Your bank lists it. Default: 4.

n.description: How often interest is added. Default: 365.

money.description: Money you put in. US dollars. Optional. Shows one year of interest. Default: 10000.

fed.description: Your federal tax rate. Shows what you keep after tax. Default: 0.

state.description: Your state tax rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Empty if left out.

tools.name: project_dividend_income
tools.description: Dividend Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How much do my shares pay in dividends? A dividend is cash a company pays the people who own its shares. The yield is how much it pays each year, as a share of the price. It starts at 4%, a made-up example. It multiplies your money by the yield you type, year by year. Dividends can be reinvested or taken as cash. It does not know what any company will pay. Dividends can be cut. People ask for it as "dividend calculator", "how to calculate dividends" or "how much to live off dividends".

amount.description: Money in it now. US dollars. Default: 20000.

yield.description: Dividend yield. A percent: 5 means 5%. Yearly dividend ÷ share price. Default: 4.

add.description: Money you add each month. US dollars. Default: 0.

growth.description: Dividend growth each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. How much the dividend rises each year. Default: 0.

payout.description: What each dividend does. Default: reinvest.

priceGrowth.description: Share price growth each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. 0% keeps the price flat. Default: 0.

tax.description: Tax on dividends. A percent: 5 means 5%. The share of each dividend paid in tax. Default: 0.

tools.name: calculate_average_cost
tools.description: Stock Average Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What did your shares cost on average? Bought the same stock more than once? Type each buy. You get your average cost for one share. It adds up what you paid for every buy and divides by your total shares. It also shows what one more buy would do. It does not say whether to buy more. People ask for it as "stock average calculator", "average down calculator" or "how to calculate average stock price".

p1.description: Price per share, buy 1. US dollars. Default: 40.

p2.description: Price per share, buy 2. US dollars. Default: 52.

p3.description: Price per share, buy 3. US dollars. Default: 34.

now.description: Price per share now. US dollars. Shows your profit or loss. Default: 30.

target.description: Average you want to reach. US dollars. Shares to buy at the price now. Default: 36.

tools.name: calculate_cagr
tools.description: CAGR Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How fast did it grow each year? CAGR means compound annual growth rate. It is the one steady rate a year that takes your start value to your end value. It finds the one steady yearly rate that turns the start value into the end value over the years you type. It does not show how the value moved in between, only one steady rate. People ask for it as "cagr calculator", "how to calculate cagr" or "what is my yearly growth rate".

start.description: Value at the start. US dollars. Default: 10000.

end.description: Value at the end. US dollars. Default: 15000.

years.description: Number of years. In years. 2.5 is fine. Default: 5.

tools.name: calculate_future_value
tools.description: Future Value Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What will your money be worth later? Future value is what your money grows to by a set date, at a set rate. It grows a lump sum and regular deposits at the rate you type. Deposits go in at the start or end of each period. It does not say what rate your money will earn. People ask for it as "future value calculator", "what will my money be worth later" or "future value of investment calculator".

start.description: Money you start with. US dollars. Default: 5000.

add.description: Money you add each time. US dollars. Pick how often just below. Default: 100.

period.description: How often you add money. Default: 12.

rate.description: Interest rate each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Treasury bills averaged 3.4% a year, 1928–2025. Default: 3.4.

years.description: How many years. In years. Default: 15.

timing.description: When you add money. At the start earns a bit more. Default: end.

tools.name: calculate_option_profit
tools.description: Options Profit Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. When does your option make money? Enter your option. See the breakeven price and the most you can lose on the last day. It works out the profit or loss on the option’s last day at the stock price you pick, and the breakeven price. It does not say what a stock will do. Options are risky: you can lose all you paid. People ask for it as "options profit calculator", "options calculator" or "how to calculate options profit".

t.description: What did you do?. A call gains if the stock goes up. A put gains if it goes down. Default: call.

k.description: Strike price. US dollars. The share price written in the contract. Default: 100.

p.description: Price you paid per share. US dollars. Option prices are per share. One contract is 100 shares. Default: 5.

got.description: Price you got per share. US dollars. You get this when you sell. One contract is 100 shares. Default: 3.

at.description: Stock price on the last day. US dollars. Optional. Shows your profit or loss at that price. Empty if left out.

fee.description: Fees, all together. US dollars. Default: 0.

sell.description: Sold an option instead?. Covered call adds one box: what you paid per share for your stock. Default: none.

b.description: What you paid per share for your stock. US dollars. Default: 100.

tools.name: calculate_roi
tools.description: ROI Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What was my return on investment? ROI is how much you made or lost compared with what you put in. It compares what you got back with what you put in. It shows the total return and the return per year. It does not say what any investment will return. People ask for it as "roi calculator", "how to calculate return on investment" or "how do i calculate roi".

in.description: Money you put in. US dollars. Default: 10000.

back.description: Money you got back. US dollars. What it is worth now, or what you sold it for. Default: 15000.

y.description: Years you held it. In years. Optional. Adds the ROI per year. Default: 5.

inc.description: Money it paid you along the way. US dollars. Such as dividends or rent you kept as cash. Default: 0.

cost.description: Extra costs. US dollars. Such as fees or repairs. They count as money you put in. Default: 0.

tools.name: estimate_capital_gains_tax
tools.description: Capital Gains Tax Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What is the tax on your gain? Enter what you paid, what you sold it for and your income. See the 2026 federal tax, long term and short term. It estimates 2026 US federal tax on one sale, long term and short term, using IRS figures. It is not tax advice. Ask a tax professional about your own return. People ask for it as "capital gains tax calculator", "how much is capital gains tax" or "capital gains calculator".

paid.description: What you paid. US dollars. Include any fees you paid to buy. Default: 10000.

sold.description: What you sold it for. US dollars. Default: 20000.

long.description: Did you own it more than a year?. Default: 1.

inc.description: Your income this year. US dollars. Taxable income: your income minus deductions. Leave out this sale. Default: 60000.

fs.description: How you file your taxes. Default: single.

magi.description: Income for the 3.8% tax. US dollars. Your modified adjusted gross income, with this sale. Leave blank and we estimate it. Empty if left out.

st.description: Your state’s tax rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Optional. We use one flat rate. Many states have brackets. Default: 0.

tools.name: replay_voo_returns
tools.description: VOO Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What did money in VOO grow to? Put in an amount and the month you put it in. See what it was really worth, with dividends put back in. It replays VOO’s real month-end closing prices for the dates shown. It shows the past only. It does not say what will happen next. People ask for it as "voo calculator", "voo investment calculator" or "voo return calculator".

start.description: Money you put in. US dollars. Default: 10000.

ago.description: When you put it in. Default: 120.

monthly.description: Money you add each month. US dollars. Buys VOO at the end of each month after your start. Dividends are always put back in. Default: 0.

tools.name: find_fire_number
tools.description: FIRE Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. When can you stop working? FIRE means you saved enough to live on, so work is a choice. We test your plan on real market years since 1928. It divides your yearly spending by the share you plan to take out each year. It runs your plan through every complete stretch of real US market years since 1928. It does not promise the money will last. The future can be worse than any past year. People ask for it as "fire calculator", "fire number calculator" or "what is my fire number".

pay.description: Take-home pay each year. US dollars. After tax. Add a partner’s pay too. Default: 75000.

spend.description: What you spend each year. US dollars. Default: 45000.

saved.description: Money saved now. US dollars. Default: 50000.

stocks.description: Share of savings in stocks. A percent: 5 means 5%. The rest is in US bonds. Default: 60.

wr.description: Share you take out each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Most people use 4%. Default: 4.

later.description: Spending each year after you stop. US dollars. Leave empty if it stays the same. Empty if left out.

tools.name: find_coast_fire_number
tools.description: Coast FIRE Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. When can you stop saving for retirement? Save enough early, and your money can grow on its own until you retire. That amount is your Coast number. It finds the amount that could grow to your retirement goal by your retirement age with no new deposits. It does not say what your money will earn. The growth rate is one you pick. People ask for it as "coast fire calculator", "how to calculate coast fire number" or "when can i stop saving for retirement".

retire.description: Age you want to retire. In years. Default: 65.

invested.description: Money saved now. US dollars. Default: 100000.

add.description: Money you add each month. US dollars. Default: 1500.

spend.description: Spending each month when retired. US dollars. Default: 4500.

growth.description: Growth each year, after inflation. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 5.

wr.description: Share you take out each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Most people use 4%. Default: 4.

other.description: Other income each month. US dollars. Like Social Security or a pension. Default: 0.

otherAge.description: Age other income starts. In years. Default: 67.

tools.name: plan_retirement_spending
tools.description: Withdrawal Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How long will your money last? Add money while you work. Take money out later. See how long it lasts. It adds money while you work and takes it out later. It runs your plan through every complete stretch of real US market years since 1928. It does not promise the money will last. The future can be worse than any past year. People ask for it as "how long will my savings last", "how long will my money last in retirement" or "retirement withdrawal calculator".

balance.description: Money invested now. US dollars. Default: 250000.

add.description: Money you add each month. US dollars. Default: 1500.

take.description: Money you take out each month. US dollars. In today’s money. It keeps up with prices. Default: 4000.

takeAge.description: Age you start taking money out. In years. Default: 62.

grow.description: Grow like. Each is a real past average, 1928–2025. Default: m60.

rate.description: Growth each year, after inflation. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 4.

stopAge.description: Age you stop adding money. In years. Leave blank to stop when you start taking money out. Default: undefined.

endAge.description: Plan until age. In years. Default: 95.

tools.name: project_roth_ira
tools.description: Roth IRA Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How much could your Roth IRA grow? A Roth IRA is a retirement account you open yourself. You pay tax on the money first, so growth can come out tax-free later. It grows yearly Roth IRA deposits at the rate you pick, up to the IRS limit. It also checks the 2026 income limit. It does not say what your money will earn. The growth rate is one you pick. People ask for it as "roth ira calculator", "roth ira growth calculator" or "how much will my roth ira be worth".

add.description: Money you put in each year. US dollars. The most for 2026 is $7,500, or $8,600 at 50 or older. Default: 5000.

retire.description: Age you want to retire. In years. Default: 65.

bal.description: Money in your Roth IRA now. US dollars. Default: 0.

grow.description: Grow like. Your own rate, or a past average used for the future. Default: own.

rate.description: Growth each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. A guess, not a promise. Default: 6.

status.description: Check if your income lets you put in. Head of household counts as single. Married, filing apart, and lived apart all year? Pick single. Default: single.

income.description: Your income for the year. US dollars. Leave blank to skip. The IRS uses modified AGI, your income after some set deductions. Empty if left out.

now.description: Your tax rate now. A percent: 5 means 5%. Empty if left out.

later.description: Your tax rate when you retire. A percent: 5 means 5%. Fill both to compare with a traditional IRA. Empty if left out.

tools.name: project_401k
tools.description: 401(k) Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What could your 401(k) grow to? See what your 401(k) could grow to by the time you retire. A 401(k) is a savings plan you get through work. It grows your deposits and your employer’s match at the rate you pick, within the IRS limits. It does not say what your money will earn. The growth rate is one you pick. People ask for it as "401k calculator", "401k contribution calculator" or "how much will my 401k be worth".

retire.description: Age you want to retire. In years. Default: 65.

pay.description: Your pay each year. US dollars. Default: 100000.

you.description: Part of your pay you put in. A percent: 5 means 5%. The IRS caps it at $24,500 in 2026, more from age 50. Default: 10.

bal.description: Money in your 401(k) now. US dollars. Default: 20000.

match.description: Your boss adds. A percent: 5 means 5%. This is called a match. Default: 50.

upto.description: Your boss stops adding at. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 6.

grow.description: Grow like. Each is a real past average, 1928–2025. Default: own.

rate.description: Growth each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. A guess, not a promise. Default: 6.

raise.description: Pay raise each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 0.

real.description: Show money in. Today’s dollars take out rising prices: 3% a year, the 1928–2025 average. Default: future.

tools.name: calculate_rmd
tools.description: Required Minimum Distribution (RMD) Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What is your 2026 RMD? Enter your age and your balance. See the least you must take out this year. It divides your balance at the end of last year by the IRS life-expectancy number for your age. It is not tax advice. Ask a tax professional about your own case. People ask for it as "required minimum distribution calculator", "rmd calculator" or "how do i calculate my rmd".

age.description: Your age at the end of 2026. In years. Default: 75.

balance.description: Money in the account on Dec 31, 2025. US dollars. It is on your year-end statement. Default: 500000.

spouse.description: Is your spouse your only heir and over 10 years younger?. "Yes" asks for their age and uses the IRS joint table. Default: no.

spouseAge.description: Your spouse's age at the end of 2026. In years. Default: 60.

working.description: Do you still work for this 401(k)'s company?. Some plans let you wait until you retire. Default: no.

grow.description: Growth each year, to see future RMDs. A percent: 5 means 5%. Your own guess. Blank shows the IRS share by age. Empty if left out.

tools.name: check_monthly_budget
tools.description: Budget Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. Where does your money go each month? Type your take-home pay and what you spend. See what is left, and how it fits the 50/30/20 rule. It takes your spending from your take-home pay. Then it compares the split to a rule of thumb like 50/30/20. It does not see your bank account. It only adds the numbers you type. People ask for it as "budget calculator", "monthly budget calculator" or "how to make a budget".

pay.description: Take-home pay each month. US dollars. Pay after taxes and deductions Default: 5000.

rent.description: Rent or mortgage. US dollars. Default: 1500.

transport.description: Getting around (car, gas, bus). US dollars. Default: 450.

wants.description: Wants. US dollars. Eating out, fun, shopping, travel Default: 900.

savings.description: Savings and extra debt payments. US dollars. Money you put away each month Default: 700.

utilities.description: Power, phone and internet. US dollars. Default: 300.

health.description: Health. US dollars. Insurance you pay, doctor, medicine Default: 200.

minDebt.description: Minimum debt payments. US dollars. The least you must pay each month Default: 150.

tools.name: plan_college_savings
tools.description: College Savings Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How much should you save for college? Pick a kind of school. See how much to save each month so your savings can pay the bills. It grows today’s school prices from US Department of Education data to the start year, then finds a monthly amount. It does not say what college will cost. Prices can rise faster than in the past. People ask for it as "529 calculator", "college savings calculator" or "how much should i save for college".

cost.description: Cost of one year of college. US dollars. See average prices in the (i) Default: 24286.

saved.description: Saved so far. US dollars. Default: 0.

monthly.description: You save each month. US dollars. Default: 300.

rate.description: Yearly return to test. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 3.4.

growth.description: Price growth each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 4.

share.description: Share of the cost you will pay. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 100.

startAge.description: Age college starts. In years. Default: 18.

years.description: Years in college. In years. Default: 4.

stepUp.description: Raise deposits each year. A percent: 5 means 5%. Your monthly amount grows this much yearly Default: 0.

keep.description: Keep saving during college. Default: no.

tools.name: plan_mortgage_payoff
tools.description: Mortgage Payoff Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How much sooner could I pay off my mortgage? Extra money goes straight to what you owe, so the loan ends sooner. It runs the loan month by month. Extra money goes straight to what you owe. It does not count taxes, insurance or fees in the payment. People ask for it as "mortgage payoff calculator", "mortgage calculator with extra payments" or "how to pay off mortgage faster".

balance.description: Loan balance left. US dollars. What you still owe. It is on your statement. Default: 300000.

rate.description: Interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 6.5.

extra.description: Extra each month. US dollars. Default: 200.

yearly.description: Extra once a year. US dollars. Like a yearly bonus. Paid with every 12th payment. Default: 0.

once.description: Extra one time, now. US dollars. Paid with your next payment. Default: 0.

often.description: How often you pay. Every 2 weeks counts as one-twelfth of your payment more each month. Default: month.

tools.name: build_amortization_schedule
tools.description: Amortization Schedule Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. What is my monthly payment? Each payment pays the interest first. The rest pays down what you owe. It finds the fixed monthly payment for the loan. Each month, interest is paid first and the rest pays down the loan. It does not count taxes, insurance or fees in the payment. People ask for it as "amortization schedule calculator", "mortgage amortization calculator" or "loan amortization calculator".

amount.description: Amount you borrow. US dollars. Default: 300000.

rate.description: Interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 6.5.

years.description: Years to pay it back. In years. Home loans are often 15 or 30 years. Car loans are often 5. Default: 30.

extra.description: Extra each month. US dollars. For more ways to pay early, use the mortgage payoff calculator. Default: 0.

tools.name: plan_credit_card_payoff
tools.description: Credit Card Payoff Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. How long to pay off your card? See when your card is paid off. See how much interest you pay on the way. Each month it adds interest at your APR, then takes off your payment, until the card is paid off. It does not know your card’s fees or future rate changes. People ask for it as "pay off credit card calculator", "credit card interest calculator" or "how to pay off credit card debt".

bal.description: What you owe on the card. US dollars. Default: 5000.

apr.description: Interest rate (APR). A percent: 5 means 5%. It is on your statement. Default: 22.

pay.description: What you pay each month. US dollars. Default: 200.

months.description: Pay it off by a date instead. In months. We show what to pay each month to be done by then. Empty if left out.

min.description: Compare with the minimum payment. Uses 1% of what you owe plus interest, at least $41. Your card's rule may differ. Default: hide.

charges.description: New charges each month. US dollars. Default: 0.

tools.name: plan_debt_snowball
tools.description: Debt Snowball Calculator with a chart, the same math as the web page. When will you be debt-free? List your debts. Compare two ways to pay them off: smallest first, or highest rate first. It pays every minimum, then puts extra money on one debt at a time. It compares smallest debt first with highest rate first. It does not say which way is right for you. People ask for it as "debt payoff calculator", "debt snowball calculator" or "debt avalanche calculator".

b1.description: Debt 1: what you owe. US dollars. Each debt: what you owe, its rate, its minimum. Default: 1500.

r1.description: Debt 1: interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 28.

m1.description: Debt 1: minimum each month. US dollars. Default: 45.

b2.description: Debt 2: what you owe. US dollars. Default: 2000.

r2.description: Debt 2: interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 6.

m2.description: Debt 2: minimum each month. US dollars. Default: 150.

b3.description: Debt 3: what you owe. US dollars. Default: 6000.

r3.description: Debt 3: interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Default: 22.

m3.description: Debt 3: minimum each month. US dollars. Default: 180.

extra.description: Extra you can pay each month. US dollars. Default: 200.

b4.description: Debt 4: what you owe. US dollars. Empty if left out.

r4.description: Debt 4: interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Empty if left out.

m4.description: Debt 4: minimum each month. US dollars. Empty if left out.

b5.description: Debt 5: what you owe. US dollars. Empty if left out.

r5.description: Debt 5: interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Empty if left out.

m5.description: Debt 5: minimum each month. US dollars. Empty if left out.

b6.description: Debt 6: what you owe. US dollars. Empty if left out.

r6.description: Debt 6: interest rate. A percent: 5 means 5%. Empty if left out.

m6.description: Debt 6: minimum each month. US dollars. Empty if left out.

only.description: Compare with paying only the minimums. Default: hide.

tools.name: search_stocks
tools.description: Finds US stocks and funds by ticker or company name. Used by the calculator card's stock picker.

query.description: A ticker or part of a company name.

tools.name: card_event
tools.description: Records which control was clicked on the calculator card. Used by the card's buttons.

calculator.description: The tool whose card it was.
